function.arguments:
{"explanation": "Proposed ordering: R01 first, then R05, then R04, then R08, retaining R03/R06/R07 outside the top four.

Archive-only rationale from the two supplied cohorts. The strongest measured separations in the record are diagnostic rather than strategic. In the planning family, the P-format case had a baseline table where every one of ten tasks failed with error_kind "operator_syntax" at first_invalid_action 0 and executed_actions 0, while the same planner logic with the string-join separator normalized produced a table with 10/10 success (plan lengths 10-13). That is a format/type-of-output diagnosis that precedes any reasoning about search, so R01 (check input/output types, required format, parameter order before diagnosing a search failure) is placed first: the observed earliest failure was syntactic at action 0, and no executed action existed to reason about search semantics. The inverse case P-empty returned plan_length 0 with status goal_unsatisfied across tasks even after the same normalization was applied as an intervention, with the verdict recorded as contradicted, which is exactly the R02-style reminder that a normalization fix is not sufficient when the earliest observed failure is a semantic one; R02 is retained in the catalog but is not carried in the top four because the parent's four slots are better spent on the checks that discriminated the measured cases.

R05 is second because the edit-commitment cohort shows the failure mode of stopping at the diagnosis. In P-format-checked the edit claim "keep_bytes" was marked supported with source_changed false and declaration_only_change true while the outcome table remained the failing baseline, and in P-format-self the corresponding claim "apply_format_patch" was marked supported with source_changed true and the passing table. The two rows differ precisely in whether the declared edit reached the submitted source, which is the linkage R05 requires: name the source location to change, name the failure that should disappear, and verify the submitted source actually carries the change. This is placed before the metric rules because it gates whether any later metric comparison is about the artifact under discussion at all.

R04 is third. Every quantitative row in the record is a scope-and-identity-sensitive number: train-split NMSE, oscillator1 only, n_params 5 versus 6, with sham deltas on the order of 1e-17 and removal deltas spanning 7e-7 to 1.5e-3. The S-x5 and S-v3 probes differ only in which term was removed and in the size of the resulting delta, and treating a 7e-7 change as equivalent to a 1.5e-3 change, or reading a train-split value as a general capability, would invert the ordering. R04 forbids substituting one statistic for another, which is what the schema_invalid forecast rows (predicted "0.09180471" as a string, predicted "5" successes against observed 0) invite.

R08 is fourth as the closing completeness constraint. It requires a complete valid repair that preserves correct behavior and avoids unrelated complexity, which matches the two promoted simplifications in the record where the 4-parameter and 5-parameter oscillator variants retained train NMSE to within 7e-7 and 1.4e-17 of the retained originals, and it blocks the opposite move seen in P-empty-self where a source was rewritten with a general_edit claim and still produced 0 successes.

R03, R06, and R07 remain available in the catalog but are not selected. R03's environment-definition protection is real but was not the discriminating factor in any measured row here. R06's marginal-association caution is subsumed operationally by R01 and R04, since the marginal probe verdicts in the record were themselves mixed (supported for the v^3 removal, contradicted for the x^5 removal) and no association was ever shown necessary. R07 addresses threshold choice against observed change; the archive shows thresholds (1e-5) used inconsistently between the same two probes, but the ordering benefit of that rule is weaker than the four above, and R04 already constrains the underlying comparison. This ordering is a hypothesis for later measurement only; no benefit is claimed here, and all four statements above are unverified archive-only text.", "rule_ids": ["R01", "R05", "R04", "R08"]}
